title: Microsoft Purview DSPM: Copilot readiness and data explorer
summary: Hold: the briefing says nothing changes data unless an administrator acts, although Microsoft has not stated the new experiences' default behaviour. Roadmap facts and the existing DSPM navigation paths are supported, but the claim that oversharing usually stalls Copilot rollouts and the categorical exclusion of end users are not established.

claims.claim: Oversharing is the usual reason a Copilot rollout stalls.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot oversharing usual most common reason rollout stalls. Read DSPM oversharing and search excerpts from Data protection and auditing for Microsoft Copilot and SharePoint readiness guidance; they establish risk, not frequency of stalled rollouts.
claims.fix: Replace 'Oversharing is the usual reason a Copilot rollout stalls' with 'Oversharing is a risk to address before a Copilot rollout', supported by https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/data-security-posture-management-oversharing.

claims.claim: If nobody acts nothing breaks, and nothing reaches users or changes data unless an administrator acts.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot readiness DSPM by default; DSPM readiness enable default permissions licensing. Read roadmap and DSPM overview and considerations; none states what the new experiences do on arrival or that administrator action is required.
claims.fix: Replace 'If nobody acts, nothing breaks: the roadmap describes insight and investigation views, not enforcement' with 'Microsoft has not stated what happens on arrival; the roadmap describes insight and investigation views and does not say existing behaviour changes.' In the risk rationale replace 'so nothing reaches users or changes data unless an admin acts' with 'and no source says existing behaviour changes'.

claims.claim: End users and makers will not see these views.
claims.quote: Searched: DSPM data explorer roles; DSPM readiness enable default permissions licensing. Read roadmap and DSPM permissions; data security teams are the intended audience, but no source categorically excludes end users or makers from the new views.
claims.fix: Remove 'end users and makers will not see these views' from the impact rationale. In Scope replace 'and the audience is data security and compliance administrators rather than end users' with 'and the roadmap describes the new experiences as capabilities for data security teams'.
